requirement:
The CSS outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rule set | `rule` | Whitespace-normalized selector list |
| Media or supports statement | `media` or `supports` | Whitespace-normalized prelude |
| Keyframes | `keyframes` | Animation name |

Nested rules appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.css.items`. They assert exact kinds and selectors, not just that the code runs.

- **Rule sets (`rule`, whitespace-normalized selector list):** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[css_profile_names_rules_by_normalized_selectors]` uses a selector list split across lines, `a  >  b,\n.x`. It asserts the name `rule[a%20>%20b,%20.x]`. The duplicate-names test in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` uses `a  b` and `a b` and asserts both normalize to `rule[a%20b]`.
- **`media` and `supports` (whitespace-normalized prelude):**
  - `css_media_and_supports_preludes_collapse_whitespace` feeds preludes with extra spaces, a tab and a newline, such as `@media  \t(max-width:\n  600px)` and `@supports  (display:  grid)`. It asserts the kinds `media` and `supports` and the collapsed selectors `media[(max-width:%20600px)]` and `supports[(display:%20grid)]`.
  - The profile test checks the same constructs with ordinary spacing.
- **`keyframes` (animation name):** The profile test asserts `keyframes[spin]`. The duplicate-names test asserts `keyframes[spin]#1` and `#2`.
- **Nested rules beneath the nearest enclosing item:** The profile test, the prelude test and the duplicate-names test all assert paths such as `media[...]/rule[a]` and `supports[...]/rule[a]`. The duplicate-names test also asserts `media[print]#2/rule[a]`, so a nested rule is attributed to the correct numbered parent. It also checks that `select` resolves to the right text.
- **Other constructs:** The profile test includes a comment and an `@import`. Neither produces an item, so the item table is not over-produced. The `from` frame inside `@keyframes` also produces no item.
- **Selector grammar, percent encoding and duplicate suffixes:** These are governed by the cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. The tests exercise them in this CSS context: `%20` encoding, `#1` and `#2` suffixes, duplicates numbered within each parent, and the bare name failing to select.

I read the implementation in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/css.rs#<root>` only to check whether deeper nesting needs its own test. The profile declares the item kinds and names. Nesting comes from the generic engine, so a case such as a rule inside a media block inside a supports block has no distinct logic to test.
